title: Dog Catches a Flying Frisbee
tests: Tests text-to-video generation of one readable action with a visible, physically coherent catch in a single shot.

faults.what: The supplied frames show the dog running with an empty mouth, then carrying a red frisbee; no airborne frisbee approaching the dog or actual catch is visible.

judge.summary: A realistic golden retriever runs through a grassy park and ends with a red frisbee in its mouth, but the requested flight and catch are not demonstrated.

must_haves.item: A realistic golden retriever is visible in a grassy park.
must_haves.why: The dog, grass, trees, and distant park visitors are clearly visible and generally realistic.

must_haves.item: A red frisbee visibly travels toward the dog before being caught in its mouth.
must_haves.why: No approaching frisbee is visible in the supplied frames; it is only seen already in the dog's mouth at 4.5 seconds.

must_haves.item: The frisbee remains identifiable through the catch rather than disappearing or passing through the dog.
must_haves.why: The frisbee is identifiable in the final frame, but the catch itself falls between the supplied frames.

must_haves.item: The five-second widescreen clip is one continuous shot with a stationary camera.
must_haves.why: The clip is listed as 5.2 seconds, the frames are widescreen, and the consistent background framing supports a continuous stationary-camera shot.
Still frames provide no evidence about the audio track.
